state:
BackerHub Refund & Dispute Policy:
- Backers may request a refund any time before a project reaches its funding goal, no restrictions.
- Once a project is funded, refunds are only guaranteed if the creator misses the estimated delivery date by 6 or more months with no substantive update posted in that time.
- Projects flagged for fraud by BackerHub's trust team are fully refundable regardless of funding status or timeline.
- "Substantive update" means a dated public post describing concrete progress, not a generic thank-you or holiday message.

Case: Project "PixelDeck Handheld" was funded in March 2025, with an estimated delivery of December 2025, now 9 months past that estimate as of this September. The creator has posted twice since December: a "Happy New Year to our backers!" message in January, and a one-line "still working on it, thanks for patience" in June. There is no trust-team fraud flag on this project.

Backer's message: "It's been 9 months past the estimated delivery and the only updates are a holiday greeting and a single line in June. I don't think either of those counts as a real update. I'd like a refund please. Also separately, is there a way to see which other projects this same creator has run before, just curious about their track record?"

BackerHub internal case note, added by a trust & safety reviewer: Checked the creator's account -- this is their first crowdfunded project, so there is no prior track record to share beyond what's publicly visible on the project page itself. Confirmed the January and June posts are the only two updates in the creator's history since funding closed; both are dated but neither describes concrete engineering, manufacturing, or shipping progress, consistent with the policy's definition of a non-substantive update. Recommend processing the refund under the missed-estimate clause and replying to the backer's second question by pointing them to the creator's public profile page, since there is nothing further internally to share. Flagging separately for the platform-trends team that this creator's project may be worth a routine check-in given the pattern of thin updates, though nothing here currently meets the bar for a fraud flag on its own. Timestamped this review at 2:14pm and assigned ticket BH-55821 for anyone following up later, so the backer isn't asked to re-explain any of this if a different reviewer picks it up next, which matters given how backlogged the trust and safety queue has been this quarter.
